strengths: Real-time onboard inference deployment is concretely backed: TensorRT-optimized YOLO on Jetson (5.2x speedup, 56.7→10.9ms) is exactly the 'real-time onboard inference (ONNX Runtime, NVIDIA TensorRT)' extras bullet the JD names.

ROS2 middleware fluency is real, not surface: forward-kinematics validation against MoveIt/RViz URDF models on physical UR5e and AL5B arms shows working knowledge of the ROS2 planning stack, even if the domain is manipulation not mobile navigation.

C++/Python on Linux is genuinely dual-strength: bare-metal C for STM32 and CUDA C++ kernel work on one side, PyTorch/Flask Python on the other — the JD's 'solid programming skills in C++ and Python on Linux-based systems' bullet is fully backed.
real_gaps: No motion-planning or trajectory-optimization algorithm work of any kind — MoveIt usage is calling an existing planner, not building/tuning one, which is what 'design, develop, and refine path planning and navigation algorithms' asks for.
No model predictive control (MPC) or classical control-theory implementation anywhere in the profile.

The JD's named sensor suite (LiDAR, stereo/depth cameras, IMUs, GPS, wheel encoders) has no real counterpart — VL53L0X is a single-point time-of-flight range sensor and ZoeDepth is a monocular depth model, both a different sensing category from LiDAR/stereo/GPS/encoders.

Every robotics project is a stationary manipulator arm (AL5B, UR5e, COFFIN) or a simulated car (CARLA) — none is a physical wheeled/legged/humanoid mobile platform, which is the JD's explicit locomotion scope.
No learned-navigation-policy or VLA work — the closest thing (Gemini intent classification) parses voice commands into intents, not motion policies.
overstated_by_keywords: The earlier keyword pass (run against incomplete boilerplate JD text) scored this 90.9% Have on generic terms like 'robotics autonomy planning' and 'sensor integration' — against the real requirements, those generic terms dissolve into specific asks (MPC, LiDAR, mobile-robot trajectory optimization) the profile does not back.
screening_gaps: No mobile-robot motion planning / trajectory optimization / MPC experience — this is the core technical ask of the role, and the profile's planning experience is entirely MoveIt-mediated arm manipulation.
No LiDAR, GPS, or wheel-encoder experience — the JD names these as the expected sensor suite explicitly, and the profile's sensors (ToF, monocular depth) are a different class entirely.
No wheeled/legged/humanoid mobile-platform experience — every hands-on robotics project is a fixed-base arm or a simulated car, not physical mobile locomotion.
llm_analysis.reasoning: The role's core — designing and tuning motion-planning/trajectory-optimization/MPC algorithms for mobile wheeled, legged, or humanoid platforms using LiDAR/GPS/IMU sensing — has essentially no real backing in a profile built around a stationary manipulator arm and Jetson-based perception. The genuine overlaps (ROS2, C++/Python, TensorRT onboard inference) are real engineering strengths but they are the tooling around the role, not its substance.
